# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The `playground` spec delivers spec #8 — the final spec in the decomposition: a sandbox section for self-contained "small-web" mini-apps, toys, games, and curiosities. Each item is its own independent thing that doesn't warrant its own repo, CI/CD, or domain. The section provides a gallery/listing of available items, and each item loads in its own space (product.md §7).

This spec builds **on top of** the CSS-isolation foundation that spec #1 (`site-foundation`) already scaffolded and validated. The site-foundation spike concluded outcome **(b) "viable with restrictions"** (`.spec-workflow/specs/site-foundation/spike-results.md`): same-page isolation via an `all: initial` reset container plus an `@layer playground` token re-declaration works, and same-page rendering is **not** cut (the spike-failure/iframe-only contingency is not triggered). Two restrictions are inherited and must be handled by this spec:

- **M1 — typography re-establishment is currently broken.** The unlayered `.playground-container { all: initial }` reset beats the layered `font-family`/`font-size`/`line-height`/`color` re-declarations inside `@layer playground` (unlayered rules win over layered rules on the same selector). Custom properties (the shadcn token path) are unaffected and work correctly. The spike pinned this bug with a broken-state test assertion. This spec must fix it.
- **M2 — shadcn/ui overlay wrappers portal to `document.body`.** No wrapper forwards a `container` prop, so overlays escape the isolation boundary unless explicitly contained. This is a per-item decision, not a global fix.

### Current state (verified against the codebase)

These artifacts already exist from `site-foundation` and are **extended in place, not rebuilt**:

- `src/app/(playground)/layout.tsx` — wraps children in `<div class="playground-container">`. The `all: initial` reset stays exactly as-is (spike directive).
- `src/styles/playground.css` — unlayered reset block + `@layer playground` block re-declaring typography and the shadcn token set (mirrored from `tokens.css :root`, light-only by design). The token block is correct; the typography block needs the M1 fix.
- `src/styles/globals.css` — declares `@layer playground;` before `@import "tailwindcss"`, placing the playground layer below Tailwind's layers (so Tailwind utilities correctly win inside the container). This spec does **not** modify this ordering.
- `src/app/(playground)/playground/page.tsx` — a chrome-less placeholder gallery page (`robots: { index: false }`), under the `(playground)` route group (no site header/nav/footer). This spec replaces the placeholder body.
- `src/app/(playground)/spike/` — the spike fixture (`page.tsx`, `spike-overlays.tsx`). May be kept as a regression harness or removed once real items provide equivalent coverage (Decision #7).
- `next.config.ts` — playground routes **already opt out of CSP** via the negative-lookahead source `/((?!playground(?:/|$)).*)`. The permissive playground CSP from the decomposition is therefore already in place; this spec verifies it and does **not** re-add it.
- `e2e/tests/playground-isolation.test.ts` — the isolation regression suite, including `INTENDED_PLAYGROUND_FONT_FRAGMENT = "ui-sans-serif"` used as a `not.toContain` broken-state marker (line ~243). When M1 lands, that assertion inverts to `toContain` (spike "Test-file fallout" guidance).
- `src/app/sitemap.ts` (XML) lists `/playground`; `src/config/site.ts` `heroCards` links to `/playground`.

### Explicitly in scope at launch

1. A typed **playground manifest** (`src/app/(playground)/playground/manifest.ts`) as the single source of truth for the gallery, `generateStaticParams`, and per-item loading.
2. The **gallery/index page** at `/playground`, rendering one card per manifest entry.
3. A **per-item landing route** `/playground/[slug]` that renders the item — inline (same-page mode) or via an iframe (iframe mode), driven by the manifest.
4. An **iframe embed route** `/playground/[slug]/embed` for items that need a separate browsing context.
5. The **M1 typography fix** in `playground.css`, with the broken-state test assertion inverted.
6. A **CSS Modules** convention for same-page item styles, plus the no-global-CSS authorship constraint.
7. **Two sample items** — one per isolation mode — that genuinely exercise the architecture (conflicting colors/fonts/layout), not hello-world divs.
8. Metadata/SEO/indexing for the new routes.
9. Build-time integrity tests (manifest↔route parity, isolation regression) and prod-build/Vercel-preview verification.
10. An **authoring doc** for adding a playground item, gated by the existing `scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs`.

### Explicitly out of scope at launch

- **Playground backends / API routes** (`/api/playground/[item]/`). Items launch client-side only; server capability is evaluated per-item later (tech.md "Server-side convention", product.md §7 "potentially with its own backend"). Not built here.
- **pnpm workspace extraction** for dependency-conflicting items (tech.md decision #7 — reserved, not a casual fallback). Conflicting items use iframe isolation instead.
- **Per-item entries in the XML sitemap.** The gallery (`/playground`) is in the XML sitemap; individual items are discoverable via the gallery's internal links (Decision #6). This mirrors how blog taxonomy permutations are excluded from XML in `slash-pages`.
- **Search indexing of playground items.** Pagefind indexes static HTML; dynamic playground content is intentionally not indexed (tech.md "Search scope").
- **Per-item dark/light theming.** Playground items control their own presentation and do not inherit the site theme (product.md §10); the container is pinned light by design.

## Alignment with Product Vision

- **Key Feature §7 (Playground):** delivers the gallery + per-item "own space" loading for self-contained experiments.
- **Design principle "Playground extensibility":** the manifest + authoring doc make adding an item a localized, documented change with no site restructuring.
- **Design principle "Progressive complexity":** the main site stays static/pre-rendered; the playground allows per-item architectures (same-page or iframe) without affecting the rest of the site.
- **Target user #4 (Matthew):** the site must be straightforward to extend with new playground items — the manifest is one entry, the item is one colocated module/folder.

## Shared Definitions (referenced by multiple requirements)

- **Manifest entry**: `{ slug, title, description, isolation: "same-page" | "iframe", load }` where `slug` is a URL-safe kebab-case string unique across the manifest, and `load` is the means of importing the item's component (e.g. a `() => import(...)` thunk consumed by `next/dynamic`). The exact shape is finalized in design; this is the contract.
- **Same-page item**: rendered inline inside `.playground-container` at `/playground/[slug]`, styled with CSS Modules, sharing the Next.js runtime/bundle.
- **iframe item**: rendered at `/playground/[slug]` as an `<iframe src="/playground/[slug]/embed">`; the item's real content lives at the embed route and runs in its own browsing context.
- **Isolation boundary**: the `.playground-container` element established by `src/app/(playground)/layout.tsx`.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: Playground manifest (single source of truth)

**User Story:** As the site maintainer, I want a single typed manifest describing every playground item, so that the gallery, static-params generation, and per-item loading never drift out of sync.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the manifest module (`src/app/(playground)/playground/manifest.ts`) is imported THEN it SHALL export a typed array of manifest entries and an exported `PlaygroundItem` type used by all consumers.
2. The manifest SHALL be the **only** place item metadata is declared; the gallery, `generateStaticParams`, and the `[slug]` loader SHALL all derive from it (no parallel hand-maintained list).
3. IF two entries share a `slug` THEN this SHALL be caught by a build-time/test integrity check (Req 10), never produce a route collision silently.
4. WHEN an entry declares `isolation: "iframe"` THEN the manifest SHALL still provide the means to render the item at the embed route (the same item module is consumed by the embed host).

### Requirement 2: Gallery / index page

**User Story:** As a visitor, I want a gallery of playground items, so that I can browse and open the experiments.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor loads `/playground` THEN the system SHALL render one card per manifest entry, each showing the item's title and description and linking to `/playground/[slug]`.
2. The gallery SHALL render inside the `.playground-container` isolation boundary (it is part of the `(playground)` route group, chrome-less by the existing layout) and SHALL use the shadcn `Card` primitive (proven to work inside the container by the spike, AC3).
3. WHEN the manifest is empty THEN the gallery SHALL render a graceful empty state, not a build error or a blank page.
4. The gallery SHALL provide a visible link back to the main site (the chrome-less layout has no site nav), consistent with the existing placeholder's "Return home" affordance.
5. The gallery SHALL be statically generated (server component).

### Requirement 3: Per-item landing route with same-page rendering

**User Story:** As a visitor, I want each playground item to open at its own URL, so that items are linkable and load in their own space.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor loads `/playground/[slug]` for a slug present in the manifest with `isolation: "same-page"` THEN the system SHALL render the item's component inline inside `.playground-container`.
2. WHEN a visitor loads `/playground/[slug]` for a slug **not** present in the manifest THEN the system SHALL return the framework 404 (`notFound()`), not a blank or crashing page.
3. The item component SHALL be loaded via dynamic import (`next/dynamic`) keyed off the manifest entry, so that one item's code is not bundled into unrelated routes.
4. `generateStaticParams` SHALL enumerate every manifest slug so all item routes are statically generated at build time.
5. WHEN a same-page item mounts a shadcn/ui overlay (Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Select, DropdownMenu) THEN the author SHALL apply the M2 containment decision rule: contain the portal (Tier 1 exported `*Portal` with `container`, or Tier 2 Radix primitive `Portal`) only when the overlay must render against playground-scoped tokens; otherwise accept the `document.body` escape (the simpler default).

### Requirement 4: iframe isolation path

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want an iframe-isolation path for items that need their own browsing context, so that items with viewport-escaping or conflicting global behavior don't break the host page.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor loads `/playground/[slug]` for a manifest entry with `isolation: "iframe"` THEN the host route SHALL render an `<iframe>` whose `src` is `/playground/[slug]/embed`.
2. The embed route SHALL live at `src/app/(playground)/playground/[slug]/embed/page.tsx` — **under `/playground/`** so it inherits the permissive (CSP-exempt) playground policy, and SHALL NOT be placed under `/api/` (tech.md "Full isolation (iframe)").
3. WHEN the embed route renders THEN it SHALL render the item's full content as the document body of the framed context, with no site chrome.
4. The iframe SHALL carry an accessible `title` attribute and a sensible default size/aspect, and SHALL be keyboard-reachable.
5. `generateStaticParams` for the embed route SHALL enumerate the iframe-mode slugs (so embed pages are statically generated); a same-page-only slug SHALL NOT produce an embed route hit (its embed path 404s).

### Requirement 5: Style-isolation foundation and the M1 typography fix

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want same-page items to render against a known, site-independent baseline, so that the site's styles don't leak in and the item's styles don't leak out.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL keep the existing two-part strategy: the unlayered `.playground-container { all: initial; isolation: isolate; … }` reset, and the `@layer playground` token re-declaration. The reset SHALL NOT be weakened.
2. The system SHALL fix M1 so the intended `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, …` font stack (and `font-size`/`line-height`/`color`) actually applies inside `.playground-container` — by the spike's preferred approach (move typography re-establishment to a second **unlayered** rule after the reset) or an equivalent higher-specificity fix; the shadcn token re-declarations SHALL remain layered (so Tailwind utilities still win).
3. WHEN M1 is fixed THEN the broken-state marker in `e2e/tests/playground-isolation.test.ts` (`INTENDED_PLAYGROUND_FONT_FRAGMENT`, currently asserted with `not.toContain`) SHALL be inverted to assert the playground stack **is** present, and the stale "broken-state marker" comment removed.
4. WHEN the host site is in dark mode AND a same-page item is open THEN the item SHALL continue to render against the playground's light tokens (the container does not inherit the site theme) — preserving the spike's verified behavior.
5. The host-leak guard (`HOST_FONT_FAMILY_FRAGMENTS`, asserting site-only fonts do NOT appear inside the container) SHALL remain in place and continue to pass.

### Requirement 6: CSS Modules scoping for same-page items

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want same-page item styles scoped so multiple items can't collide, so that adding an item is safe.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a same-page item needs styles THEN it SHALL author them in a colocated CSS Module (`*.module.css`) so class names are hashed and collision-free.
2. Playground item styles SHALL NOT write global CSS rules or unscoped selectors (tech.md constraint). This is enforced by authorship convention and documented in the authoring doc (Req 11); no automated linter is required at launch.
3. The authoring doc SHALL state where item modules live (colocated under the playground route group in a non-route private folder, e.g. `_items/<slug>/`, so item modules are not themselves routable) and how the manifest references them.

### Requirement 7: Sample items (one per isolation mode)

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want one real sample item in each isolation mode shipped at launch, so that the architecture is proven end-to-end and there is a copyable template.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The launch set SHALL include at least one **same-page** item and one **iframe** item, both functional.
2. The same-page sample SHALL set colors, fonts, and layout properties that would visibly conflict with the main site theme (proving the reset + CSS Modules genuinely isolate), per the decomposition's "trivial hello-world divs don't exercise the isolation architecture."
3. The iframe sample SHALL exercise a pattern that justifies iframe isolation (e.g. its own document-level styling / viewport-escaping behavior), demonstrating the full-isolation path.
4. WHEN either sample is opened from the gallery THEN it SHALL render correctly with no visual leakage from or into the surrounding context.

### Requirement 8: Metadata, SEO, and indexing

**User Story:** As Matthew, I want the playground routes titled and indexed appropriately, so that the section is discoverable but iframe internals aren't surfaced as standalone pages.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The gallery `/playground` SHALL be **indexable** (flip the placeholder's `robots: { index: false }` to indexable) and SHALL export `generateMetadata()` with the site title template and default OG image (cross-spec metadata convention). It is already present in the XML sitemap.
2. Each `/playground/[slug]` landing route SHALL export per-item metadata (title/description from the manifest entry) and SHALL be indexable.
3. Each `/playground/[slug]/embed` route SHALL be `robots: { index: false }` (it is an iframe target, not a standalone destination) and SHALL NOT appear in the XML sitemap.
4. The system SHALL NOT advertise any `noindex` route in the XML sitemap (the consistency rule established in `slash-pages` Decision #3).

### Requirement 9: Security and CSP

**User Story:** As Matthew, I want the playground's relaxed CSP scoped to playground routes only, so that the rest of the site keeps its protective CSP.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL rely on the **existing** route-scoped CSP opt-out for `/playground/*` in `next.config.ts` (negative-lookahead source `/((?!playground(?:/|$)).*)`); this spec SHALL NOT re-add or duplicate that rule, and SHALL NOT relax CSP for any non-playground route.
2. WHEN the iframe host (`/playground/[slug]`) embeds `/playground/[slug]/embed` THEN the same-origin embed SHALL load without a CSP/framing error (both routes are under the CSP-exempt playground path).
3. Playground items SHALL have no authentication, no stored user data, and no sensitive operations at launch (tech.md acceptance rationale for the relaxed CSP).
4. WHERE a playground item renders external resources or inline code, this is permitted only because it is first-party and CSP-exempt; the authoring doc SHALL note that items are first-party-only.

### Requirement 10: Build-time integrity and test coverage

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want tests that fail loudly when the playground wiring regresses, so that adding or renaming items can't silently break routing or isolation.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL have a test asserting manifest↔route integrity: every manifest slug resolves to a `/playground/[slug]` route, slugs are unique, and iframe-mode slugs resolve to an embed route.
2. The system SHALL retain and update the isolation regression suite (`e2e/tests/playground-isolation.test.ts`), including the inverted M1 assertion (Req 5.3) and the retained host-leak guard (Req 5.5).
3. The system SHALL include an E2E that opens each sample item from the gallery and asserts it renders (same-page item visible inside the container; iframe item's `<iframe>` present and its embed document loads).
4. WHEN the isolation suite is run THEN it SHALL be run against a **production build** (Webpack), since `@layer` ordering and CSS Modules hashing can differ between Turbopack (dev) and Webpack (prod) (tech.md known issue); item isolation SHALL additionally be verified on a Vercel preview deploy before merge.
5. The E2E suite SHALL assert that `/playground` and `/playground/[slug]` serve **no** `Content-Security-Policy` header (confirming the route-scope opt-out still holds), consistent with the existing CSP E2E in `site-foundation`.

### Requirement 11: Authoring documentation

**User Story:** As the maintainer (and future me), I want a documented procedure for adding a playground item, so that extending the section is a localized, repeatable change.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The system SHALL add `docs/playground-authoring.md` documenting: how to pick an isolation mode (the tech.md "when in doubt, use iframe" rule and the patterns that require iframe), where item modules live, how to add a manifest entry, the CSS Modules + no-global-CSS constraint, and the M2 overlay-containment decision rule.
2. The authoring doc SHALL be gated by the existing `scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs` (added to its doc-list, the same drift protection the `slash-pages` and `contributions-and-resources` docs use); the script's self-test (`scripts/check-authoring-docs.test.mjs`) SHALL be updated if the doc-list change affects it.
3. The authoring doc SHALL state the launch constraints: client-side only, no playground backend, first-party items only.

## Decisions (resolved during requirements authoring)

1. **Same-page isolation is viable and used** — per the spec-1 spike outcome (b). The iframe-only contingency (spike failure path) is **not** triggered; both isolation modes ship. (Source: `spike-results.md`.)
2. **Manifest is code, not Velite** — playground items are code modules with per-item architecture, not MDX/YAML content, so the single source of truth is a typed `manifest.ts`, not a Velite collection. This is the decomposition's stated pattern ("`playground/manifest.ts` … single source of truth for `generateStaticParams`, gallery, and dynamic import").
3. **Every item has a `/playground/[slug]` landing route** — same-page items render inline there; iframe items render an `<iframe>` to `/playground/[slug]/embed` there. This gives one consistent, linkable URL per item regardless of isolation mode, and keeps the embed route under `/playground/` for the CSP exemption.
4. **M1 fixed via unlayered typography re-establishment** (spike's preferred option) — keeps the token path layered (so Tailwind utilities win) while giving typography the specificity it needs. The broken-state test marker inverts when this lands. (Source: `spike-results.md` M1.)
5. **M2 handled per-item, default to `document.body` escape** — contain overlay portals only when the overlay must render against playground-scoped tokens; otherwise accept the simpler default. Captured as an authoring rule, not a global mechanism. (Source: `spike-results.md` M2.)
6. **XML sitemap lists the gallery only** — per-item routes are discoverable via the gallery's internal links, not enumerated in `src/app/sitemap.ts`. Avoids coupling `sitemap.ts` to the manifest for marginal SEO benefit; mirrors the `slash-pages` choice to exclude taxonomy permutations. Embed routes are `noindex` and excluded.
7. **Spike fixture removal is optional** — `src/app/(playground)/spike/` may be removed once the sample items + regression suite provide equivalent coverage, or kept as a harness. Not forced either way; whichever the design phase chooses, the isolation regression coverage (Req 10.2) must not regress.
8. **CSP opt-out is reused, not rebuilt** — site-foundation already scoped CSP off for `/playground/*`; this spec verifies it (Req 9, Req 10.5) and does not touch the rule.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- **Single Responsibility**: `manifest.ts` holds item metadata (data only); `[slug]/page.tsx` owns same-page-vs-iframe routing + metadata; `[slug]/embed/page.tsx` owns the embed render; item modules own item behavior + their CSS Module; `playground.css`/`layout.tsx` own the isolation boundary.
- **Modular Design**: each playground item is self-contained in its own colocated module/folder; adding one touches the manifest plus the item folder and nothing else.
- **Dependency Management**: items share the single dependency tree (tech.md decision #7); items whose dependencies conflict use iframe isolation rather than workspace extraction.
- **Clear Interfaces**: the `PlaygroundItem` type is exported from `manifest.ts` and is the contract used by the gallery, both route hosts, and `generateStaticParams`.

### Performance

- The gallery and item landing routes are statically generated server components; item code loads via dynamic import so it isn't bundled into unrelated routes.
- **Lighthouse performance target: 90+** on the gallery, verified at launch (cross-spec performance-baseline convention). Individual interactive items are exempt from the strict budget where their own architecture dictates (product.md §95 progressive-complexity), but SHALL not regress the gallery.

### Security

- Relaxed CSP is scoped to `/playground/*` only; the rest of the site keeps its protective CSP unchanged.
- Items are first-party, client-side, with no auth or stored data at launch.
- External `target="_blank"` links inside items SHALL use `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

### Reliability

- An unknown `[slug]` SHALL 404 via `notFound()`, never crash or render blank.
- An empty manifest SHALL produce a graceful empty gallery, not a build error.
- Manifest↔route integrity and isolation regressions SHALL fail CI (Req 10).

### Usability

- The gallery and same-page items render correctly with WCAG 2.1 AA contrast within the playground's light token set.
- iframes carry an accessible `title` and are keyboard-reachable.
- The gallery provides a visible path back to the main site.

### Accessibility

- The gallery uses semantic landmarks and a single `<h1>`; item cards use accessible link names.
- Each item landing route has a single `<h1>` (the item title) or an item-appropriate heading structure.
- WCAG 2.1 AA violations on the new playground pages are blocking issues (cross-spec accessibility convention); items that intentionally subvert conventions (games/toys) document any deviations in the authoring doc.

### Maintainability

- Adding a playground item is: one manifest entry + one colocated item module (+ embed-mode flag) — no site restructuring.
- The authoring doc (Req 11) is the single source of authoring truth and is drift-gated by `scripts/check-authoring-docs.mjs`.
- Cross-document citations use stable symbol/file references rather than volatile line numbers where practical.
